# p0_servicenow_ai (Resource)

A ServiceNow instance installation for agentic access.

Installing it allows P0 to grant agents ServiceNow roles on a machine user for each gateway session.

**Important:** Before creating this resource you must stage the installation with `p0_servicenow_ai_staged`, deploy the connector's Cloud Run service, and add the client secrets and signing key as a version of the connector's install secret. Creating this resource verifies that the connector can sign in to the instance and read its roles.

**Note:** This integration is currently in preview.

For the full install steps, see [ServiceNow](https://docs.p0.dev/integrations/resource-integrations/agentic-gateway/mcp-server/servicenow).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Installs a ServiceNow instance for agentic access, with P0's ServiceNow
# connector on Cloud Run and its client secrets and signing key in Google
# Secret Manager. Set up the provisioner and JWT bearer inbound integrations on
# the instance first.
# Full chain: p0_gcp -> p0_servicenow_ai_staged -> Cloud Run connector and
# install secret -> install secret version (added outside Terraform) ->
# p0_servicenow_ai.

resource "p0_gcp" "example" {
  organization_id = "123456789012"
}

locals {
  project = "my-project-id"
  # The instance name, as in acme.service-now.com
  instance = "acme"
  # P0 reads the client secrets and signing key from the secret with this
  # exact ID.
  install_secret_id = "p0_install_servicenow_${local.instance}_install"
}

resource "p0_servicenow_ai_staged" "example" {
  id = local.instance

  secret_manager = {
    type       = "gcp-sm"
    project_id = local.project
  }

  depends_on = [p0_gcp.example]
}

resource "google_project_service" "enable_services" {
  for_each = toset([
    "cloudresourcemanager.googleapis.com",
    "iam.googleapis.com",
    "run.googleapis.com",
    "secretmanager.googleapis.com",
  ])
  project            = local.project
  service            = each.key
  disable_on_destroy = false
}

resource "google_service_account" "connector" {
  project      = local.project
  account_id   = split("@", p0_servicenow_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.connector_service_account)[0]
  display_name = "P0 Cloud Run ServiceNow connector"

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service" "connector" {
  project             = local.project
  name                = p0_servicenow_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.connector_service_name
  location            = p0_servicenow_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.connector_region
  deletion_protection = false
  # P0 calls the connector from outside GCP; IAM, not origin, gates access.
  ingress = "INGRESS_TRAFFIC_ALL"

  template {
    service_account = google_service_account.connector.email

    containers {
      image = "docker.io/p0security/p0-connector-servicenow-ai-gcloud:sha-2fd68a0@sha256:935ecc126a3cc57eeb73081b9bde5ef7df99ed6e231cd71531a67f5609aefba7"

      # The connector also checks this against the caller's OIDC token.
      env {
        name  = "INVOKER_SA_EMAIL"
        value = p0_gcp.example.service_account_email
      }
    }
  }

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member" "invoke_connector" {
  project  = local.project
  location = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.location
  name     = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.name
  role     = "roles/run.invoker"
  member   = "serviceAccount:${p0_gcp.example.service_account_email}"
}

# P0 reads the service to get its invocation URL while it installs. The invoker
# role gives run.routes.invoke only, so it cannot do this read.
resource "google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member" "read_connector" {
  project  = local.project
  location = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.location
  name     = google_cloud_run_v2_service.connector.name
  role     = "roles/run.viewer"
  member   = "serviceAccount:${p0_gcp.example.service_account_email}"
}

data "google_project" "this" {
  project_id = local.project
}

# The connector keeps each session's token in its own secret. GCP checks
# secretmanager.secrets.create on the project, so this binding has no condition.
resource "google_project_iam_custom_role" "connector_secret_create" {
  project     = local.project
  role_id     = "p0ServiceNowConnectorSecretCreate"
  title       = "P0 ServiceNow connector secret creation"
  permissions = ["secretmanager.secrets.create"]

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_project_iam_member" "connector_secret_create" {
  project = local.project
  role    = google_project_iam_custom_role.connector_secret_create.name
  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"
}

resource "google_project_iam_custom_role" "connector_secret_manage" {
  project = local.project
  role_id = "p0ServiceNowConnectorSecretManage"
  title   = "P0 ServiceNow connector access token management"
  permissions = [
    "secretmanager.secrets.delete",
    "secretmanager.secrets.get",
    "secretmanager.versions.add",
  ]

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_project_iam_member" "connector_secret_manage" {
  project = local.project
  role    = google_project_iam_custom_role.connector_secret_manage.name
  member  = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"

  # P0 names the session token secrets with this prefix. IAM conditions use the
  # project number, not the project ID.
  condition {
    title      = "P0 ServiceNow access token secrets"
    expression = "resource.name.startsWith('projects/${data.google_project.this.number}/secrets/p0_access-token_servicenow_${local.instance}_')"
  }
}

# After apply, add the two client secrets and the signing private key as one
# JSON version of this secret, before you create p0_servicenow_ai:
#
#   jq -n \
#     --arg provisionerClientSecret "$SN_PROVISIONER_CLIENT_SECRET" \
#     --arg jwtClientSecret "$SN_JWT_CLIENT_SECRET" \
#     --rawfile signingKey p0-servicenow-signing-key.pem \
#     '$ARGS.named' \
#     | gcloud secrets versions add p0_install_servicenow_acme_install \
#       --project=my-project-id --data-file=-
resource "google_secret_manager_secret" "install" {
  project   = local.project
  secret_id = local.install_secret_id

  replication {
    auto {}
  }

  depends_on = [google_project_service.enable_services]
}

resource "google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member" "install" {
  project   = local.project
  secret_id = google_secret_manager_secret.install.secret_id
  role      = "roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor"
  member    = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"
}

# The accessor role gives secretmanager.versions.access only. The connector also
# reads the secret itself, and the management role above covers the session
# token secrets alone, so the install secret needs its own grant.
resource "google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member" "install_read" {
  project   = local.project
  secret_id = google_secret_manager_secret.install.secret_id
  role      = "roles/secretmanager.viewer"
  member    = "serviceAccount:${google_service_account.connector.email}"
}

# Completes the install; creating it verifies that the connector can sign in to
# the instance as the provisioner and read its roles.
resource "p0_servicenow_ai" "example" {
  id = p0_servicenow_ai_staged.example.id
  # Client IDs of the instance's two inbound integrations, and the kid of the
  # signing certificate in the JWT bearer integration's verifier map.
  provisioner_client_id = "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"
  jwt_client_id         = "fedcba9876543210fedcba9876543210"
  key_id                = "p0-signing"

  secret_manager = {
    type       = p0_servicenow_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.type
    project_id = p0_servicenow_ai_staged.example.secret_manager.project_id
  }

  depends_on = [
    google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member.invoke_connector,
    google_cloud_run_v2_service_iam_member.read_connector,
    google_project_iam_member.connector_secret_create,
    google_project_iam_member.connector_secret_manage,
    google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member.install,
    google_secret_manager_secret_iam_member.install_read,
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) The `id` of the `p0_servicenow_ai_staged` resource being finalized
- `jwt_client_id` (String) The client ID of the JWT bearer integration that trusts the connector's signing certificate. The connector gets each agent user's token with it.
- `key_id` (String) The `kid` of the signing certificate in the JWT bearer integration's verifier map
- `provisioner_client_id` (String) The client ID of the client credential integration whose OAuth application user has only `user_admin`. The connector signs in with it to manage agent users.
- `secret_manager` (Attributes) Where P0's ServiceNow connector runs and stores its client secrets, signing key, and session tokens (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--secret_manager))

### Read-Only

- `state` (String) This item's install progress in the P0 application:
	- 'stage': The item has been staged for installation
	- 'configure': The item is available to be added to P0, and may be configured
	- 'installed': The item is fully installed

<a id="nestedatt--secret_manager"></a>
### Nested Schema for `secret_manager`

Required:

- `project_id` (String) The GCP project that hosts the connector's Cloud Run service and the secret that holds the connector's client secrets and signing key. Must match the `p0_servicenow_ai_staged` resource.
- `type` (String) The secret manager that stores the connector's client secrets and signing key. Only `gcp-sm` (Google Secret Manager) is supported. Must match the `p0_servicenow_ai_staged` resource.

Read-Only:

- `connector_region` (String) The GCP region in which to deploy the connector's Cloud Run service
- `connector_service_account` (String) The email of the GCP service account that the connector must run as
- `connector_service_name` (String) The name to give the connector's Cloud Run service
- `connector_service_uri` (String) The invocation URL of the connector's Cloud Run service, resolved by P0 during install
